381.t: Tracking down daughter Penny in Montreal and Detroit
381.s: Using phone books, he traced Carol, learned Penny had been adopted, and met her in Detroit.
381.ch: Leaving Dinah Shore and his daughters
381.q: Her mother's name is Mary. So now I'm with a show and playing in Toronto, Canada. I had the address of Carol in Montreal.

381.t: Finding Sandra through the Platters' Tony Williams connection
381.s: A chain of contacts led to Sandra's mother, and he met Sandra and her six daughters in the Bronx.
381.ch: Leaving Dinah Shore and his daughters
381.q: so then, about nine months later, I'm looking at the TV in Los Angeles, and this black woman who is the news commentator -- her last name is Williams. Now, I had another young lady that I had the third daughter by -- her name was Tara, and her brother -- I didn't know it at the time, but her…

259.t: His children and where he was working when they were born
259.s: Vincent speaks of the babies he lost and his surviving children, who were born around 1922 to 1924, and of children he never saw on the road.
259.q: You. Have any children? Children. Children? Children? No, not living in there. Fine dies. She goes. Dive another baby. And one of the last ones, she was, oh, about a couple of hours. And I smothered. Doctor thought she had to show my wife, you know, for a particular day, I look at her baby, so big…

877.s: Russell recalls the funeral service where the brothers played, and Handy explains his mother took the name Richards from her second marriage to a preacher.
877.q: His name is Julius, right? That's right. He was there also. All of us was playing at the church at that time when she was speaking. And our, uh.

306.t: George and Emma Zeno's family; contacting Emma
306.s: Allen and Rene discuss Emma Zeno and George's children. Allen gives Rene her address and phone number.
306.ch: Joe Rene: Lewis, the Rena band and New Orleans
306.q: Oh, that's all them children... They had about four boys, yeah. Yeah, that's right. Four boys and a couple of girls. Yeah, that's the same one, eh? Yeah.

1048.s: Johnson says her children grew up with the music and that her husbands, children and relatives have all worked for The Rag.
1048.q: Well in my own family, my kids are music buffs and they grew up with the music. My son was six when I started The Rag, my daughter was three. So they were kind of mascots for the Hall Brothers Jazz Band at the Emporium of Jazz and we had musicians staying with us and they heard that music all the…

141.t: Family moves and Audre's advertising job and teaching career
141.s: The family moved to Jackson Heights and Smithtown; Audre worked in advertising, then taught for 20 years.
141.q: Yeah. My kids said, “Oh, you have to watch this.” It really was a lot like that. When I got pregnant with the second one, I had to quit, because you couldn’t work if you were pregnant. Then I went back to school when my youngest went to junior high. Then I taught for 20 years.

135.s: Heath recalls Connie Kay's real name Kirnon, wife Addie, sons Rodney and Noel and second wife Frances.
135.q: And they lived up in his mother’s house in the Bronx. Now Mr. Kay was sort of a mac daddy type and he had some other ladies later, but he left Addie and the two boys in the Bronx.

506.s: Carter talks about his sons' births, Janet's role, and bringing the children dinner at 3:30 AM.
506.q: Um … Janet probably did. I'd come home from work at night at 2 o'clock in the morning and I would stop by a restaurant and get something to eat and wake up the kids and say, Let's have something to eat. That's not a good idea at 3:30 AM, I guess. (laughs)

428.s: His children's careers, grandchildren, and the 1950 separation from his second wife.
428.q: Well, they're not connected musically. Barbara is working for a hospital. She's a Senior Health Program Analyst for the mental health hospitals of all New York, and she has a daughter, Linda, 17, still going to school, on scholarship.

413.t: Children and grandchildren and their names
413.s: His son David Evans Maxwell, daughter Anne Reid Maxwell, and the naming of his grandsons.
413.q: David, David Evans Maxwell. I gave him the middle name Evans after Gil Evans, who at that time was my best friend. Since then we've drifted apart quite a bit. But it's still a pretty name.
